primitives.name: Chiral Pass Bias Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Most importantly, if we look at the length of the wedges, we can see that right footed left backs seem more likely to pass infield whereas the left footed left backs have longer wedges leading diagonally forward (where the colour is darkest and the xT is highest).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Wedge Length: Dimensionless proportion of total pass count; xT: Expected Threat, dimensionless probability of goal scoring within a sequence; Angle: Radians relative to pitch center line.
primitives.assumptions: Passing networks are stationary over the observation window; biomechanical constraints induce a deterministic angular shift in passing vectors based on dominant foot.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down in highly constrained penalty box scenarios or when defensive pressing density exceeds a critical threshold, forcing purely reactive, low-xT clearances regardless of footedness.

primitives.name: Threat Sector Expansion Kernel

primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Sector Count: Integer representing distinct high-xT angular bins; Angular Width: Degrees of pitch coverage yielding positive xT gradients.
primitives.assumptions: Defensive spacing allows for multiple viable passing lanes; the spatial distribution of receiving teammates does not artificially cap the available angles.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities occur during deep-block defensive phases where all forward passing lanes are occluded, collapsing the threat sector expansion to zero.

primitives.name: Winger Retrograde Penalty
primitives.verbatim_quote: Right footed left wingers are much more likely to play the ball diagonally backward whereas left footers are more likely to play the ball directly infield, and with higher threat.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Retrograde Probability: Dimensionless likelihood of negative-y-axis pass displacement; Infield Threat Gradient: Delta xT per unit distance passed towards the goal line.
primitives.assumptions: Opposing midfield lines maintain a standard horizontal structure; winger positioning is strictly confined to the outer third of the pitch width.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails in inverted-winger systems where the primary objective is central dribbling rather than wide passing, decoupling footedness from retrograde passing tendencies.

layer2.mapping: Directly maps to the GSE state-transition penalty function, assigning a heavy cost to backward-diagonal edges for agents possessing mismatched chiral attributes.
